title: Bounded derived smooth base change
statement:
Use the coefficient conventions [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions]: $\Lambda$ is a finite commutative ring, $N$ is a positive integer, $(N:\Lambda)=0$, and $N$ is invertible on $S$ (equivalently its image is a unit in $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$). In a cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X&\xleftarrow{h}&Y\\
f\downarrow&&\downarrow e\\
S&\xleftarrow{g}&T,
\end{array}
$$
assume $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For every $K\in\Dbc(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], the canonical derived exchange
$$
\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(K):Lf^*Rg_*K\longrightarrow Rh_*Le^*K
$$
of [sbc-def-base-change-map] is an isomorphism in the ambient unbounded category $D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. No boundedness or constructibility of its two endpoints is asserted.

proof.text: Let $U_T$ denote derived coefficient forgetting and put $L=U_TK$. The exact conservative functor and its cohomology identifications are supplied by [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison]. Bounded constructibility [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] gives integers $a\le b$ with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$; hence $\mathcal H^q(L)=U_T\mathcal H^q(K)$ vanishes there too and $L$ is bounded below. For every element $x$ of every stalk of $\mathcal H^q(K)$, the elementary module calculation $N x=(N:\Lambda)x=0$ shows that its underlying abelian stalk is killed by the positive integer $N$. By [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions], $N$ is invertible on $S$. Thus every $\mathcal H^q(L)$ is a torsion abelian sheaf of orders invertible on $S$: if an element has order $d$, then $d\mid N$, so write $N=dm$. In $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$, the image of $d$ has inverse $mN^{-1}$, since $d(mN^{-1})=NN^{-1}=1$. Thus its order is invertible on $S$. This argument uses the module action directly and needs no stratification or extension-by-zero argument.

source.place: Tag 0D6J, lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded; coefficient calculation in the standing conventions

proof.text: For each $q$ apply [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] to the abelian sheaf $\mathcal H^q(L)$. Its allowable torsion hypothesis was checked in Step 1; the square is cartesian, $f$ is smooth, and $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the statement. For every $p\ge0$ this gives an isomorphism of the actual degreewise exchange $f^{-1}R^pg_*\mathcal H^q(L)\longrightarrow R^ph_*e^{-1}\mathcal H^q(L)$, with the degreewise map understood exactly as in [sbc-def-base-change-map].

To apply the generic abelian spectral-sequence nodes, rename their $(X_0,Y_0,X'_0,Y'_0;f_0,f'_0,g_0,g'_0)$ as $(T,S,Y,X;g,h,f,e)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-couple-morphism] to $L$: its clauses (1) and (2) supply the two exact couples and the morphism induced by the canonical bounded-below exchange, and clause (3) identifies its $E_2$ arrows with the degreewise arrows in Step 2. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-convergence] with the lower bound $a$ and the torsion cohomology verified in Step 1. Both spectral sequences vanish unless $p\ge0$ and $q\ge a$ and converge with finite filtrations in every total degree. Consequently all their $E_2$ arrows are isomorphisms: for $p\ge0$ use Step 2, and for $p<0$ both sides are zero by the cited quadrant assertion.

source.place: Tag 015J, lemma-two-ss-complex-functor; truncation-couple formulation in the cited nodes

proof.text: With this same renaming, $L\in D^+(T_{\Et})$, the bounds $[a,b]$, and the $E_2$ morphism just checked satisfy every hypothesis of [sbc-lem-finite-range-comparison]. It follows that the bounded-below abelian exchange $\operatorname{BC}^{+}_{f,g}(L)$ is an isomorphism. Now [lem-sbc-abelian-derived-exchange-plus-compatibility] identifies the unbounded abelian exchange at $L$ with the composite $Df(c_g^{-1}(L))$, followed by the bounded-below inclusion of $\operatorname{BC}^{+}_{f,g}(L)$, followed by $c_h(De^+L)$. Every factor is invertible, so $\operatorname{BC}^{\mathbf Z}_{f,g}(L)$ is invertible in the ambient abelian derived category. Only $L$ needs a finite cohomological interval; no bounded-above assertion for $Rg_*L$ or $Rh_*e^{-1}L$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0F09, lemma-smooth-base-change-general, spectral-sequence argument using Tag 015J; bounded-below/unbounded mate comparison in the cited compatibility node

proof.text: The definition [sbc-def-base-change-map] identifies the required module map with the canonical unbounded exchange on the renamed square. Apply [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison] on that square to $K$. Its canonical endpoint isomorphisms $s_K,t_K$ satisfy $t_K\circ U_X(\operatorname{BC}^{\Lambda}_{f,g}(K))=\operatorname{BC}^{\mathbf Z}_{f,g}(L)\circ s_K$. Step 4 makes the right-hand side invertible, hence $U_X(\operatorname{BC}^{\Lambda}_{f,g}(K))=t_K^{-1}\circ\operatorname{BC}^{\mathbf Z}_{f,g}(L)\circ s_K$ is invertible. The cited node states conservativity of $U_X$, so the specified module exchange itself is an isomorphism, as required.
